name: Emmer wheat
desc: One of the first domesticated cereals in the Fertile Crescent, a founder crop of Neolithic farming.

name: Einkorn wheat
desc: Diploid wheat domesticated in southeastern Anatolia, among the earliest cultivated cereals.

name: Bread wheat
desc: Hexaploid wheat from a natural cross of emmer and wild goatgrass, now the world's main wheat.

name: Barley domestication
desc: Founder crop of the Near East used for food, fodder and brewing.

name: Foxtail millet
desc: Millet domesticated in northern China, the staple of early Yellow River farming.

name: Rice domestication
desc: Domestication of Asian rice in the Yangtze valley, later the staple of much of humanity.

name: Paddy field
desc: Flooded, bunded fields for wet rice that suppress weeds and sustain high yields.

name: Soybean domestication
desc: Legume domesticated in East Asia, a major source of protein and oil.

name: Maize domestication
desc: Domestication of teosinte into maize in southern Mexico, the basis of Mesoamerican farming.

name: Potato domestication
desc: Domestication of the potato in the Andes, later a staple that fed Europe's population growth.

name: Cassava domestication
desc: Starchy root domesticated in southwestern Amazonia, now a staple across the tropics.

name: Sorghum domestication
desc: Drought-tolerant cereal domesticated in Africa.

name: Olive cultivation
desc: Domesticated olive tree of the Levant, source of oil, food and lamp fuel.

name: Viticulture
desc: Cultivation of the grapevine, begun in the South Caucasus, the basis of winemaking.

name: Sugarcane domestication
desc: Giant grass domesticated in New Guinea, later the world's main source of sugar.

name: Cotton cultivation
desc: Independent domestication of cotton in South Asia and the Americas for fibre.

name: Tea cultivation
desc: Cultivation and processing of the tea plant in China, later a global crop.

name: Coffee cultivation
desc: Roasting and brewing coffee seeds, begun in Yemen and spread worldwide as a cash crop.

name: Cacao and chocolate
desc: Fermenting and roasting cacao beans into drink, first in Mesoamerica.

name: Sheep domestication
desc: Domestication of mouflon into sheep in the Near East, for meat, milk and later wool.

name: Goat domestication
desc: Goats domesticated in the Zagros, among the first livestock.

name: Pig domestication
desc: Wild boar domesticated independently in Anatolia and China.

name: Cattle domestication
desc: Domestication of the aurochs, providing meat, milk, hides and draught power.

name: Chicken domestication
desc: Red junglefowl domesticated in Southeast Asia, now the most numerous livestock.

name: Horse domestication
desc: Taming of the horse on the Eurasian steppe for milk, riding and traction.

name: Sericulture
desc: Rearing domesticated silkworms on mulberry leaves to produce silk, begun in China.

name: Beekeeping
desc: Keeping honey bees in hives for honey and wax, shown in Egyptian reliefs.

name: Langstroth hive
desc: Hive with removable frames spaced by the bee space, the basis of modern beekeeping.

name: Pastoralism
desc: Herding livestock across pasture as a way of life, spreading farming into marginal lands.

name: Dairying
desc: Milking livestock and processing milk, shown by milk residues in Neolithic pottery.

name: Yoke
desc: Wooden beam joining draught oxen so they can pull a plough or cart.

name: Horseshoe
desc: Nailed iron shoe protecting hooves, letting horses work on hard and wet ground.

name: Horse collar
desc: Padded collar resting on the shoulders that let horses pull heavy loads without choking.

name: Systematic selective breeding
desc: Deliberate breeding for chosen traits, systematized for livestock by Robert Bakewell.

name: Artificial insemination
desc: Introducing semen without mating, first shown by Spallanzani and later central to cattle breeding.

name: Battery cage
desc: Wire cages housing laying hens in rows, enabling industrial egg production.

name: Antibiotics in livestock
desc: Routine antibiotics in feed to promote growth, which accelerated antimicrobial resistance.

name: Intensive animal farming
desc: Confining large numbers of animals indoors for industrial meat, egg and milk output.

name: Barbed wire
desc: Cheap wire fencing with sharp barbs that enclosed open rangeland.

name: Electric fence
desc: Fence delivering pulsed shocks to contain livestock cheaply.

name: Automatic milking
desc: Robotic milking systems that milk cows without a human operator.

name: Cream separator
desc: Centrifuge that separates cream from milk, industrializing butter making.

name: Sickle
desc: Curved blade for reaping cereals, first made of flint set in bone or wood.

name: Hoe
desc: Hand tool for breaking soil and weeding, the main tillage tool before the plough.

name: Quern-stone
desc: Hand-operated grinding stones for turning grain into flour.

name: Granary
desc: Dedicated storehouse for threshed grain, allowing surplus and planning.

name: Winnowing
desc: Separating grain from chaff by tossing it in the wind.

name: Threshing board
desc: Flint-studded sledge dragged by animals over grain to thresh it.

name: Scythe
desc: Long-bladed mowing tool for cutting hay and grain standing upright.

name: Heavy plough
desc: Wheeled mouldboard plough that turned heavy clay soils of northern Europe.

name: Seed drill
desc: Device that sows seeds in rows at set depth, used in Han China and improved by Jethro Tull.

name: Slash-and-burn agriculture
desc: Clearing forest by cutting and burning for temporary fields.

name: Crop rotation
desc: Alternating crops on a field to restore fertility and break pest cycles.

name: Three-field system
desc: Medieval rotation of winter grain, spring crop and fallow that raised output.

name: Norfolk four-course system
desc: Rotation of wheat, turnips, barley and clover that eliminated fallow.

name: Terrace farming
desc: Stepped fields cut into hillsides to farm slopes and control erosion.

name: Shadoof
desc: Counterweighted lever for lifting water, used in Mesopotamia and Egypt.

name: Qanat
desc: Gently sloping underground channel bringing groundwater to fields in arid Iran.

name: Noria
desc: Current-driven wheel with pots that lifts river water for irrigation.

name: Saqiyah
desc: Animal-driven geared wheel that raises water from wells and canals.

name: Chinampa
desc: Raised fields built in shallow lakes by Mesoamerican farmers, highly productive.

name: Tile drainage
desc: Buried clay pipes that drain waterlogged fields, opening wet soils to farming.

name: Windpump
desc: Self-regulating wind-driven pump that watered livestock on dry plains.

name: Center-pivot irrigation
desc: Rotating sprinkler arm watering circular fields from a central well.

name: Drip irrigation
desc: Delivering water slowly to plant roots through plastic tubing, saving water.

name: Greenhouse
desc: Glazed structure that traps heat to grow plants out of season.

name: Grafting
desc: Joining a scion to a rootstock to propagate fruit trees true to type.

name: Agricultural chemistry
desc: Liebig's chemistry of plant nutrition, which showed which minerals crops need.

name: Manuring
desc: Spreading animal dung on fields to return nutrients to the soil.

name: Guano fertilizer
desc: Seabird and bat droppings mined and shipped as a rich nitrogen and phosphate fertilizer.

name: Superphosphate
desc: Phosphate rock treated with sulfuric acid, the first manufactured fertilizer.

name: Synthetic nitrogen fertilizer
desc: Industrially made nitrogen fertilizer from ammonia, which now feeds billions.

name: Pesticide
desc: Substances that kill crop pests, from Sumerian sulfur dusts onward.

name: Biological pest control
desc: Using natural enemies against pests, from Chinese citrus ants to imported beetles.

name: Paris green
desc: Copper arsenite insecticide used against the Colorado potato beetle.

name: Bordeaux mixture
desc: Copper sulfate and lime fungicide that saved vineyards from downy mildew.

name: Lead arsenate
desc: Arsenical insecticide widely sprayed on orchards until DDT replaced it.

name: Bt biopesticide
desc: Bacterium whose insecticidal toxins were sold as a spray from 1938.

name: DDT
desc: Synthetic organochlorine insecticide whose insecticidal action was found in 1939.

name: 2,4-D
desc: First selective synthetic herbicide, killing broadleaf weeds in cereal crops.

name: Sterile insect technique
desc: Releasing irradiated sterile males to collapse pest populations.

name: Integrated pest management
desc: Combining monitoring, biological control and targeted spraying to limit pesticide use.

name: Paraquat
desc: Fast-acting contact herbicide that made no-till farming practical.

name: No-till farming
desc: Planting without ploughing, using herbicides for weeds, to cut erosion.

name: Glyphosate
desc: Broad-spectrum herbicide sold as Roundup, the most used herbicide.

name: Neonicotinoid
desc: Systemic nicotine-like insecticides, later restricted over harm to bees.

name: Scientific plant breeding
desc: Systematic crossing and selection of crops, put on a genetic footing by Mendel's pea work.

name: Hybrid corn
desc: Crossing inbred lines to exploit hybrid vigour, which raised maize yields sharply.

name: Mutation breeding
desc: Inducing mutations with radiation or chemicals to create new crop varieties.

name: Norin 10 wheat
desc: Japanese semi-dwarf wheat whose dwarfing genes underlie Green Revolution wheats.

name: Seed bank
desc: Collections of stored seed to preserve crop genetic diversity, begun by Vavilov.

name: High-yielding varieties
desc: Short-strawed crop varieties that respond to fertilizer without lodging.

name: IR8 rice
desc: Semi-dwarf 'miracle rice' from IRRI that doubled rice yields in Asia.

name: Green Revolution
desc: Spread of high-yield seed, fertilizer, pesticide and irrigation that averted famines.

name: Genetically modified crops
desc: Crops carrying engineered genes, first created as transgenic tobacco in 1983.

name: Flavr Savr tomato
desc: First commercially sold genetically engineered whole food, a slow-softening tomato.

name: Bt cotton
desc: Cotton producing Bacillus thuringiensis toxin to resist bollworms.

name: Bt maize
desc: Insect-resistant genetically modified maize, now widely grown.

name: Herbicide-tolerant soybean
desc: Glyphosate-tolerant Roundup Ready soybean, the most planted GM crop.

name: Golden rice
desc: Rice engineered to make beta-carotene to fight vitamin A deficiency.

name: Aquaculture
desc: Farming fish and other aquatic organisms, as in the Budj Bim eel traps of Australia.

name: Oyster farming
desc: Cultivating oysters on beds or ropes, practised by the Romans.

name: Fish hatchery
desc: Artificial spawning and rearing of fish to stock waters and farms.

name: Salmon farming
desc: Raising salmon in sea cages, begun at scale in Norway.

name: Aquaponics
desc: Combining fish farming with hydroponics so fish waste feeds plants.

name: AquAdvantage salmon
desc: Fast-growing genetically engineered salmon, the first GM animal approved as food.

name: Hydroponics
desc: Growing plants in mineral nutrient solutions without soil.

name: Vertical farming
desc: Growing crops in stacked indoor layers under artificial light.

name: Precision agriculture
desc: Using satellite positioning and field data to vary inputs across a field.

name: Agricultural drone
desc: Unmanned aircraft for spraying and monitoring crops, first used for rice in Japan.

name: Agricultural robot
desc: Robots that weed, pick or monitor crops autonomously.

name: Cotton gin
desc: Eli Whitney's machine for separating cotton fibre from seeds.

name: Threshing machine
desc: Andrew Meikle's machine that beat grain from straw, replacing the flail.

name: Mechanical reaper
desc: Horse-drawn machine that cut grain, commercialized by McCormick.

name: Combine harvester
desc: Machine that reaps, threshes and winnows grain in one pass.

name: Grain elevator
desc: Steam-powered bucket elevator and storage tower for bulk grain.

name: Tower silo
desc: Tall structure for storing grain or fermented fodder.

name: Silage
desc: Fermented, high-moisture fodder that keeps cattle fed through winter.

name: Traction engine
desc: Self-propelled steam engine for ploughing, threshing and haulage on farms.

name: Tractor
desc: Gasoline-powered farm vehicle that replaced draught animals.

name: Fordson tractor
desc: Mass-produced, affordable tractor that brought mechanization to small farms.

name: Three-point hitch
desc: Harry Ferguson's linkage attaching implements rigidly to a tractor's hydraulics.

name: Cotton picker
desc: Machine that harvests seed cotton, ending hand-picking in the US South.

name: Gristmill
desc: Water-powered mill grinding grain into flour.

name: Roller mill
desc: Mill that crushes grain between rollers, producing fine white flour in bulk.

name: Olive oil extraction
desc: Crushing and pressing olives to obtain oil.

name: Sugar crystallization
desc: Boiling cane juice into crystalline sugar, developed in India.

name: Beet sugar
desc: Extracting sugar from beets, first factory in Silesia in 1801.

name: High-fructose corn syrup
desc: Corn syrup converted enzymatically to fructose, a cheap industrial sweetener.

name: Food drying
desc: Preserving food by removing water in sun, wind or smoke.

name: Smoking
desc: Exposing meat and fish to smoke to dry, flavour and preserve them.

name: Salting
desc: Preserving meat and fish with salt, which draws out water.

name: Pickling
desc: Preserving food in brine or vinegar.

name: Food fermentation
desc: Using microbes to transform and preserve food and drink.

name: Beer brewing
desc: Fermenting malted cereals into beer, among the oldest prepared drinks.

name: Winemaking
desc: Fermenting grape juice into wine in pottery jars.

name: Cheesemaking
desc: Curdling and draining milk to make a storable food.

name: Bread
desc: Baking ground grain dough, first as flatbread by hunter-gatherers.

name: Leavened bread
desc: Bread raised by wild yeast and bacteria, made in ancient Egypt.

name: Noodles
desc: Strands of dough, the oldest known found at Lajia in China.

name: Nixtamalization
desc: Cooking maize in alkaline solution, which unlocks niacin and makes masa.

name: Ice house
desc: Insulated building for storing natural ice through summer.

name: Pasteurization
desc: Mild heating to kill spoilage microbes, devised by Pasteur for wine.

name: Condensed milk
desc: Milk concentrated with sugar and canned, keeping without refrigeration.

name: Baking powder
desc: Chemical leavening that releases carbon dioxide, replacing yeast for quick breads.

name: Margarine
desc: Butter substitute invented by Mège-Mouriès, later made from vegetable oils.

name: Refrigerated ship
desc: Ship with refrigerated holds that carried frozen meat across oceans.

name: Refrigerator car
desc: Insulated railcar that carried chilled meat from Chicago to eastern cities.

name: Cold chain
desc: Unbroken refrigerated supply chain, completed by refrigerated trucks.

name: Freeze drying
desc: Removing water from frozen food under vacuum by sublimation.

name: UHT processing
desc: Heating milk briefly above 135 C to sterilize it for months of storage.

name: Iodised salt
desc: Salt fortified with iodine to prevent goitre.

name: Quick-frozen food
desc: Clarence Birdseye's rapid freezing that preserved food texture.

name: Food irradiation
desc: Exposing food to ionizing radiation to kill pathogens and extend shelf life.

name: Instant noodles
desc: Pre-cooked, flash-fried noodles invented by Momofuku Ando.

name: Textured vegetable protein
desc: Defatted soy flour extruded into a meat-like texture.

name: Chorleywood bread process
desc: High-speed mixing process for fast, cheap industrial bread.

name: Aseptic packaging
desc: Filling sterilized food into sterile cartons, enabling shelf-stable milk.

name: Single-cell protein
desc: Protein from microbes grown in fermenters, tried as feed and food.

name: Mycoprotein
desc: Fungal protein grown by fermentation and sold as Quorn.

name: Fermentation-produced chymosin
desc: Rennet enzyme made by engineered microbes, the first recombinant food ingredient.

name: Cultured meat
desc: Meat grown from animal cells in culture, first shown as a burger in 2013.

name: Plant-based meat
desc: Meat analogues from plant proteins, some with fermented heme for flavour.

name: Precision fermentation
desc: Engineered microbes producing specific food proteins such as animal-free whey.

name: Cocoa powder
desc: Van Houten's pressing and alkalizing of cacao that made cocoa powder and solid chocolate possible.

name: Lentil
desc: Early domesticated legume of the Fertile Crescent that fixes nitrogen and supplied protein.

name: Common bean
desc: Legume domesticated in Mesoamerica and the Andes, part of the maize-bean-squash complex.

name: Banana cultivation
desc: Bananas cultivated in New Guinea and spread across the tropics as a staple.

name: Squash domestication
desc: Cucurbita squashes, among the first plants domesticated in the Americas.

name: Llama domestication
desc: Andean camelid domesticated from the guanaco as a pack animal and fibre source.

name: Water buffalo domestication
desc: Buffalo domesticated in South and East Asia, the draught animal of rice farming.

name: Turkey domestication
desc: Wild turkey domesticated in Mesoamerica for meat and feathers.

name: Camel domestication
desc: One-humped camel domesticated in Arabia, enabling desert herding and caravans.

name: Transhumance
desc: Seasonal movement of herds between summer and winter pastures.

name: Secondary products revolution
desc: Use of animals for milk, wool and traction rather than only meat.

name: Livestock branding
desc: Marking animals with hot irons to show ownership, recorded in ancient Egypt.

name: Butter
desc: Churning cream into a storable fat; a Sumerian tablet of about 2500 BCE describes the process.

name: Egg incubator
desc: Heated chambers for hatching eggs, used at scale in ancient Egyptian egg ovens.

name: Broiler chicken
desc: Chicken breeds selected for very fast growth, the basis of industrial meat poultry.

name: Feedlot
desc: Confined yards where cattle are fattened on grain before slaughter.

name: Mechanical sheep shearing
desc: Shearing wool with powered handpieces, first commercialized by Wolseley in Australia.

name: Semen cryopreservation
desc: Freezing semen with glycerol, which let elite bulls sire offspring worldwide.

name: Genomic selection
desc: Predicting breeding value from genome-wide markers, transforming dairy cattle breeding.

name: Harrow
desc: Implement dragged over ploughed land to break clods and cover seed.

name: Terra preta
desc: Charcoal-enriched anthropogenic soils created by Amazonian farmers.

name: Green manure
desc: Ploughing in legumes or other cover crops to enrich the soil.

name: Polder
desc: Low land enclosed by dikes and drained for farming, developed in the Low Countries.

name: Impact sprinkler
desc: Rotating sprinkler head that spreads water over fields and lawns.

name: Wardian case
desc: Sealed glass case that let living plants survive long sea voyages.

name: Mushroom cultivation
desc: Cultivating edible fungi on prepared substrates, begun at scale near Paris.

name: Potash fertilizer
desc: Potassium salts mined from deposits such as Stassfurt for fertilizer.

name: Rhizobium inoculant
desc: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria applied to legume seed, first sold as Nitragin.

name: Parathion
desc: Early organophosphate insecticide, highly effective and highly toxic.

name: Atrazine
desc: Triazine herbicide widely used on maize.

name: Pyrethroid
desc: Synthetic analogues of plant pyrethrins, stable enough for field use.

name: Aerial application
desc: Spraying or dusting crops from aircraft.

name: Triticale
desc: Wheat-rye hybrid cereal first bred in the late 19th century; fertile forms became practical after colchicine doubling in 1937.

name: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
desc: Arctic backup vault storing duplicates of the world's seed collections.

name: Marker-assisted selection
desc: Using DNA markers linked to traits to select plants and animals faster.

name: Fish pond culture
desc: Raising fish such as carp in managed ponds, practised in ancient China.

name: Cultured pearl
desc: Pearls grown by implanting a nucleus in oysters, commercialized by Mikimoto.

name: Seaweed farming
desc: Cultivating seaweeds such as nori, begun in Japan.

name: Shrimp farming
desc: Raising shrimp in ponds, pioneered by Motosaku Fujinaga in Japan.

name: Recirculating aquaculture
desc: Land-based tanks that filter and reuse water to farm fish.

name: Power take-off
desc: Drive shaft that lets a tractor power attached implements.

name: Baler
desc: Machine that compresses hay or straw into compact bales.

name: Multiple-effect evaporator
desc: Norbert Rillieux's evaporator that reused steam to refine sugar efficiently.

name: Rum
desc: Spirit distilled from sugarcane molasses on Caribbean plantations.

name: Glucose syrup
desc: Sweet syrup from acid hydrolysis of starch, found by Kirchhoff.

name: Corn wet-milling
desc: Steeping and separating maize into starch, germ and gluten on an industrial scale.

name: Meat extract
desc: Liebig's concentrated beef extract, an early industrial food.

name: Infant formula
desc: Manufactured breast-milk substitute, first marketed by Liebig.

name: Evaporated milk
desc: Unsweetened concentrated milk sterilized in cans.

name: Breakfast cereal
desc: Ready-to-eat processed grain foods, starting with granula.

name: Corn flakes
desc: Toasted flaked maize developed by the Kellogg brothers.

name: Instant coffee
desc: Dried coffee extract that dissolves in water.

name: Milk chocolate
desc: Chocolate made with milk, devised by Daniel Peter.

name: Conching
desc: Rodolphe Lindt's prolonged mixing that gave chocolate its smooth texture.

name: Monosodium glutamate
desc: Isolated umami flavour compound, later made industrially by fermentation.

name: Iodised salt
desc: Salt fortified with iodine to prevent goitre.

name: Powdered milk
desc: Milk evaporated to a dry powder for long storage.

name: Tofu
desc: Curdled soy milk pressed into blocks, a protein staple of East Asia.

name: Soy sauce
desc: Fermented soybean and grain seasoning that originated in Han China.

name: Garum
desc: Fermented fish sauce produced at industrial scale in the Roman world.

name: Tortilla
desc: Flatbread of nixtamalized maize, the staple of Mesoamerica.

name: Stockfish
desc: Unsalted cod air-dried on racks in Norway, traded across Europe.

name: Ice trade
desc: Harvesting lake ice and shipping it worldwide for cooling food.

name: Icebox
desc: Insulated cabinet cooled by blocks of ice, the domestic forerunner of the refrigerator.

name: Sliced bread
desc: Machine-sliced and wrapped bread, first sold in 1928.

name: High-pressure processing
desc: Preserving food with very high pressure instead of heat.

name: Veggie burger
desc: Commercial meatless burger patty made from vegetables, grains or soy.
